questions.question: What are the four key evaluation dimensions for recommending a tech stack?
choices: Price, Popularity, Age, and Logo color
Team capability, Project requirements, Ecosystem maturity, and Operational cost
questions.explanation: Good tech stack recommendations evaluate: can the team actually use it (capability), does it fit the project needs (requirements), is the ecosystem stable and supported (maturity), and what's the total cost of ownership (operations).

questions.question: Why should team capability be the first consideration when recommending a tech stack?
choices: Because it's the easiest dimension to evaluate
Because even the best technology fails if the team lacks the skills to use it effectively, leading to slower delivery and more bugs
Because it determines the project budget
Team capability doesn't matter when using AI coding assistants
questions.explanation: A technically superior stack that the team can't use effectively will underperform a simpler stack the team knows well. Learning curves have real costs — missed deadlines, architectural mistakes, and production incidents.

questions.question: What is the danger of recommending a tech stack based solely on benchmark performance?
choices: Benchmarks measure synthetic conditions that may not reflect real-world performance, ignoring factors like developer productivity, ecosystem support, and operational complexity
questions.explanation: Benchmarks test isolated micro-benchmarks under ideal conditions. Real-world performance depends on many factors benchmarks don't cover: developer velocity, library availability, debugging tools, deployment complexity, and community support.
